correctness.rationale: The exact 27-point coordinate model gives the two-distance strongly regular identity \(A^2=8I+2A+8J\) and adjacency eigenspace dimensions \(1,6,20\). The spherical-harmonic addition theorem converts the exact-degree evaluation Gram matrix into \(I+a_kA+b_k(J-I-A)\). The exact rational Gegenbauer table for \(0\le k\le8\) gives ranks \(1,6,20,20,26,27,27,26,27\). The Chebyshev derivative formula gives \(|P_k(t)|\le3/[(k+1)(k+2)(1-t^2)^{3/2}]\), and the strict rational envelope \(16|a_k|+10|b_k|<304/[3(k+1)(k+2)]<1\) for \(k\ge9\) makes every sector strictly positive. Exact rational row reduction of nine Gram matrices, all 729 two-distance identities and analytic-envelope rational comparisons were replayed at the actual packaged checker path. The harmonic-index list follows by the constant-sector sum-of-squares identity. Finite checking is not used to justify the infinite part.

originality.rationale: Published classical theorems contain the unique 27-point four-design and its two inner products; the newer preprints contain the general harmonic-index and addition formula. Compared to those exact statements, the complete rank sequence and isolated seventh-degree failure require a separate all-degree spectral computation and uniform Gegenbauer positivity argument. value.rationale: The unique canonical 27-point tight spherical four-design poses a natural exact-degree interpolation problem. The result determines all ranks and Gram eigenvalues, shows the first single-degree surjectivity at 5 followed by an isolated rank-26 failure at 7, establishes permanent surjectivity from degree 8, and identifies precisely the harmonic-index cancellations. These complete natural structural invariants are not isolated arbitrary evaluations; the result does not claim applications beyond this justified scope.
